Samir - thanks for the clear list. Quick recap and our recommendation after the call:

1) Recommended models to test (start small, expand):
   - rw-7b-instruct (fast/low cost, good for exact-match QA)
   - rw-13b-chat (balanced quality/latency for multi-turn underwriting prompts)
   - rw-14b-quantized (higher quality baseline - use for regression/benchmark)

We recommend running all three in parallel on the same dataset to compare latency, token cost, and quality.

2) Dataset format: CSV with the following columns (UTF-8, comma-separated):
   - id (unique row id)
   - input_text (the prompt sent to the model)
   - expected_output (the canonical answer/label)
   - metadata (optional free-text JSON string with fields: customer_id, doc_type, risk_bucket)

I've attached a small sample CSV (acme_eval_dataset.csv) and a prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.txt). We also included our redwood_eval_template.json which is a lightweight config you can use to run the eval via the Console or API.

3) Scoring & metrics we support out-of-the-box:
   - Exact match / token-level match (for deterministic responses)
   - Normalized string match (case/whitespace normalization)
   - BLEU / ROUGE for generative summaries
   - Embedding similarity (cosine) for semantic match; you can set a threshold (we usually start at 0.82 for short answers)
   - Custom scoring functions: you can plug in a scoring hook and return a pass/fail or numeric score

4) Regression & false positives:
   - Use a small stable baseline set (~100 high-value prompts) and compare new models against that set first.
   - For noisy/long-form examples, prefer embedding similarity + human-in-the-loop review to avoid spurious failures.
   - We'll surface both absolute diffs and delta alerts; tune thresholds per label type.

Next steps:
- If you can confirm the attached CSV format and share any additional metadata fields you want preserved, Neha will provision the eval workspace and run the three-model sweep.
- We'll deliver a results dashboard (latency/cost/score) and a short action memo with recommended model and suggested prompt edits.

Neha - can you take point on provisioning once Samir confirms? I'll coordinate the workshop with Rishi to walk through the dashboard.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@acmefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme Financial - eval setup & recommended models (technical details)

Hi Samir - thanks, this is straightforward. Technical details and exact steps to run on Redwood: 

1) Dataset guidelines (CSV):
   - Required columns: id, input_text, expected_output
   - Optional columns: metadata (stringified JSON), sample_weight (numeric)
   - Maximum file size for self-serve upload: 500MB; for larger sets we'll share an S3 ingest flow

2) Eval config (what we'll run):
   - For each model: generate N completions (N=1 for QA; N=3 for multi-turn/rerank experiments)
   - Post-processing: strip stop tokens, normalize whitespace, lowercase (configurable)
   - Scoring: run normalized string match AND embedding similarity (OpenAI/Redwood embeddings) and compute combined score = 0.6*normalized_match + 0.4*embedding_score (default; adjustable)

3) Quality regression checks:
   - We compute baseline score per-example and flag any with delta <= -0.05 (5 percentage points) as potential regressions.
   - For generative summaries, we also surface ROUGE-L and a human review queue for top 50 low-scoring examples.

4) How to hand off the dataset to us:
   - Quick option: upload acme_eval_dataset.csv via the Redwood Console -> Evals -> New Eval -> Upload CSV.
   - API option: POST /v1/evals with multipart form data + eval config (we included a sample curl in the attached redwood_eval_template.json).

5) Permissions & security:
   - Data at rest is encrypted. For PII-sensitive rows you can either mask PHI before upload or ask for a private deployment.
   - We will add Acme to a short-lived eval workspace and share access for a week.

Attachment notes: the redwood_eval_template.json has the example config we will use. Example scoring snippet (plain text):

  scoring:
    strategy: combined
    normalized_match_weight: 0.6
    embedding_similarity_weight: 0.4
    embedding_threshold: 0.82

If you confirm the CSV and tell us whether you want us to run synchronous or asynchronous evals (sync returns small sets quickly; async for bigger sweeps), I can provision the workspace today.

-Neha
